All architecture claims from the brief verified against the code. Here is the implementation plan. # Implementation Plan: Player Skin Presets (Appearance) ## Verified ground truth (deltas from the brief: none significant) - `createPlayerModel()` (`/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`) takes no args; 7 color constants; `skinMat` is shared by arms + skull; `HAIR` material is created inline at line 103; eye materials created at 106-107. `materials`/`geometries` arrays only. - `createPlayerVisuals(scene)` calls `createPlayerModel()` once in a closure; returns `{ sync, triggerSwing, dispose }`. - `GameRenderer` holds `private readonly playerVisuals` (line 42/86); `triggerSwing()` is the existing one-shot fan-out template. - `useMinecraftGame` audio pattern confirmed: storage-read effect (lines 83-88) runs in the first commit; the renderer effect runs in a *later* commit (ctx is set by the `attachMount` callback ref → re-render), so refs populated by the load effect are reliably available when the renderer is created. `updateAudioSettings` (90-96) is the callback template. `window.__monecraft` exposes `renderer`. - Sprite pipeline: `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts` (`SPRITE_SIZE = 16`, `paintGrid(grid, palette)` with `Rgb = [r,g,b]` and `.`/space transparent) → `lib/ui/sprites.ts` `spriteDataUrl(key, () => pixels)` with cache + happy-dom transparent fallback → `components/game/PixelImg.tsx` (hydration-safe ``). `lib/ui` already imports from `lib/game` (`ITEM_DEF_BY_ID`), so a `lib/ui` → `lib/game/playerSkins` import is consistent. - PauseMenu test style: roles/labels + `aria-pressed` (mute button), `mock()` callbacks. E2E style: `Escape` pauses directly when unlocked; assertions via `__monecraft` and `localStorage` (see `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts` save test reading `minecraft_save_v5`). --- ## New files ### 1. `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/playerSkins.ts` — presets (pure, no imports) ```ts export type PlayerPalette = { skin: number; hair: number; shirt: number; pants: number; shoes: number; eyeWhite: number; eyePupil: number; }; export type SkinPreset = { id: SkinId; label: string; palette: PlayerPalette }; export type SkinId = "default" | "alex" | "zombie" | "skeleton" | "knight" | "robot"; export const DEFAULT_SKIN_ID: SkinId = "default"; export const SKIN_PRESETS: readonly SkinPreset[] = [ ... ]; export function isSkinId(value: unknown): value is SkinId; export function getSkinPreset(id: string): SkinPreset; // unknown/corrupt id → default preset ``` The six palettes (default = the current constants, byte-for-byte): | preset | skin | hair | shirt | pants | shoes | eyeWhite | eyePupil | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Default** | `0xc68e63` | `0x4a3220` | `0x2e8b83` | `0x3b3f8f` | `0x4a3527` | `0xffffff` | `0x2b2b45` | | **Alex** | `0xe6b18a` | `0xb5602e` | `0x5f8a3a` | `0x6e5036` | `0x57422c` | `0xffffff` | `0x3f6b3a` | | **Zombie** | `0x6a9a4e` | `0x4e7a3a` | `0x2f6e62` | `0x4f4377` | `0x3d3326` | `0x1d2b1d` | `0x0a120a` | | **Skeleton** | `0xdcdcd2` | `0xc4c4ba` | `0xb1b1a7` | `0x9a9a90` | `0x83837a` | `0x2e2e2e` | `0x121212` | | **Knight** | `0xaab2bd` | `0x7c8591` | `0x8d96a3` | `0x646d79` | `0x4a525c` | `0x161a20` | `0x161a20` | | **Robot** | `0x767f8a` | `0x4d545e` | `0x5b636d` | `0x444b54` | `0x32373e` | `0x35e9ff` | `0x0b6f80` | Design notes: Knight's eyeWhite == eyePupil intentionally renders a continuous dark visor slit across both eye boxes. Robot's bright cyan eyeWhite reads as a glow at this material roughness; a true `emissive` channel is a deliberate v2 omission (would complicate `setPalette` to color-only swaps). Zombie keeps the MC zombie read: green skin, darker teal shirt than Default, faded purple pants, near-black eyes. ### 2. `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/skinSettings.ts` — persistence (mirror `lib/game/audio/settings.ts` exactly) ```ts export const SKIN_SETTINGS_KEY = "minecraft_skin_v1"; export type SkinSettings = { skinId: SkinId }; // object, not bare string — forward-compat export const DEFAULT_SKIN_SETTINGS: SkinSettings = { skinId: DEFAULT_SKIN_ID }; export function readSkinSettings(storage: Storage = localStorage): SkinSettings; // try/catch, isSkinId-validate, fallback default export function writeSkinSettings(settings: SkinSettings, storage: Storage = localStorage): void; // silent catch ``` ### 3. `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/ui/skinPortrait.ts` — bust portrait pixels (pure, bun-testable) ```ts export function renderSkinPortraitPixels(palette: PlayerPalette): Uint8ClampedArray; ``` Implementation: convert hex → `Rgb` (`[(hex>>16)&255, (hex>>8)&255, hex&255]`), derive shades (`shade(rgb, 0.75)` for skin shadow `S` and shirt hem `T`), then `paintGrid(BUST_GRID, {...})`. Suggested 16×16 grid (legend: `h` hair, `s` skin, `S` skin-shadow, `w` eyeWhite, `p` pupil, `t` shirt, `T` shirt-shadow): ``` "................" "...hhhhhhhhhh..." "...hhhhhhhhhh..." "...hhhhhhhhhh..." "...hssssssssh..." "...ssssssssss..." "...sswwsswwss..." "...sswpsspwss..." "...ssssssssss..." "...sssSSSSsss..." "....SssssssS...." "......ssss......" "......SssS......" ".tttttttttttttt." "tttttttttttttttt" "TTTTTTTTTTTTTTTT" ``` ### 4. Tests: `lib/game/playerSkins.test.ts`, `lib/game/skinSettings.test.ts`, `lib/ui/skinPortrait.test.ts` (details in commit slices). --- ## Modified files ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/playerModel.ts` - Delete the 7 module constants; import `DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE` (add it as a named export of `playerSkins.ts` — alias of the default preset's palette) and `type PlayerPalette`. - Signature: `createPlayerModel(palette: PlayerPalette = DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE): PlayerModel` — zero churn for existing call sites and all 4 existing tests. - Extend `PlayerModel` with `paletteMaterials: Record` (the same instances also stay in `materials` for disposal — no double-dispose risk, `materials` remains the single disposal authority). Name the inline hair material; keep `material(color)` helper but collect the 7 into the record. - Add `export function applyPalette(model: PlayerModel, palette: PlayerPalette): void` — `for (const key of keys) model.paletteMaterials[key].color.setHex(palette[key])`. No material/geometry allocation; live-safe. ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/playerVisuals.ts` - Add `setPalette(palette: PlayerPalette): void` to the `PlayerVisuals` type, implemented as `applyPalette(model, palette)`. - Do **not** add a constructor param (design Q4 decision): the renderer effect calls `setPlayerSkin` synchronously after `GameRenderer.create` and before the first `requestAnimationFrame`, so no rendered frame can show the default palette. Also the body boots invisible (first-person + `visible = false`). Constructor param rejected as churn without observable benefit. ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts` - Add next to `triggerSwing()` (line ~119): ```ts setPlayerSkin(palette: PlayerPalette): void { this.playerVisuals.setPalette(palette); } ``` - Renderer stays id-agnostic (takes a palette, not a `SkinId`); the hook resolves id → palette. Keeps render code decoupled from preference plumbing. ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts` Mirror the audio pattern, plus one new ref because skin needs the renderer (audio has `audioRef`; there is no renderer ref today): - State: `const [skinId, setSkinId] = useState(DEFAULT_SKIN_ID);` + `skinIdRef` + new `rendererRef = useRef(null)`. - Extend the existing post-mount storage effect (lines 83-88) — same effect, not a new one: `const { skinId: storedSkin } = readSkinSettings(); skinIdRef.current = storedSkin; queueMicrotask(() => setSkinId(storedSkin));` (renderer doesn't exist yet in this commit — ordering argument above). - In the renderer effect, right after `canvasRef.current = renderer.domElement;`: `rendererRef.current = renderer; renderer.setPlayerSkin(getSkinPreset(skinIdRef.current).palette);` Cleanup: `rendererRef.current = null;` alongside `canvasRef.current = null`. - Callback: ```ts const updateSkin = useCallback((id: SkinId) => { skinIdRef.current = id; setSkinId(id); writeSkinSettings({ skinId: id }); rendererRef.current?.setPlayerSkin(getSkinPreset(id).palette); }, []); ``` - Return `skinId, updateSkin`. ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/lib/ui/sprites.ts` ```ts export function skinPortraitUrl(skinId: SkinId): string { return spriteDataUrl(`skin:${skinId}`, () => renderSkinPortraitPixels(getSkinPreset(skinId).palette)); } ``` (Reuses the cache and the happy-dom transparent-pixel degradation for free.) ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/game/PauseMenu.tsx` - Props: `skinId: SkinId; onSkinChange: (id: SkinId) => void;` - New section between `.pause-sound` and the save message: ```tsx
Appearance
{SKIN_PRESETS.map((preset) => ( ))}
``` (Image is decorative — the button's `aria-label` carries the name, matching test-by-role conventions; never assert pixels in component tests.) ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/components/MinecraftGame.tsx` Pass `skinId={skinId} onSkinChange={updateSkin}` into `` (line ~101) from the hook return. ### `/Users/hutusi/workspace/ai/david/monecraft/app/hud.css` After `.pause-sound` block (~line 71): `.pause-skins` (grid, gap 8px, margin-top 4px), `.pause-skins-title` (reuse `var(--mc-text-light)` + `var(--mc-text-shadow)`, font-weight 700), `.pause-skins-grid` (`grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 6px;`), `.skin-swatch` (column flex, mc-button bevel recipe: `background: var(--mc-button)`, the same 2px `#a8a8a8/#2c2c2c` border-color trick, hover → `var(--mc-button-hover)`), `.skin-swatch[aria-pressed="true"]` (highlight border, e.g. gold `#f0be3c` bevel + brighter background) so the selected state is style-driven off the accessible attribute. ### Docs - `CHANGELOG.md`: user-facing entry. - `README.md`: mention skin presets in the features list (it lists audio settings; follow suit). - `docs/adding-content.md`: short "Adding a skin preset" note (add a `SKIN_PRESETS` entry; the integrity tests force portrait coverage automatically). --- ## Commit slices **Slice 1 — `Add player skin presets and persisted skin selection`** Files: `lib/game/playerSkins.ts`, `lib/game/skinSettings.ts`, both tests. Why-body: skins are a render/UI preference like audio volumes, not world state, so they get their own validated localStorage key (`minecraft_skin_v1`) and a presets module both the renderer and React shell can import without touching the engine. Stored as `{ skinId }` so future appearance fields don't need a key migration. Tests: presets — 6 entries, unique ids, `getSkinPreset("nope")` → default, `DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE` equals the default preset palette. Settings — Map-backed fake `Storage` (copy the shape from `lib/game/audio/settings.test.ts`): roundtrip, missing key → default, corrupt JSON → default, unknown id → default, throwing `setItem` swallowed. **Slice 2 — `Parameterize the player body palette and recolor it live`** Files: `playerModel.ts`, `playerVisuals.ts`, `GameRenderer.ts`, `playerModel.test.ts` (+2 tests), `playerVisuals.test.ts` (+1). Why-body: the body's colors were burned in as module constants; threading a `PlayerPalette` through and exposing the seven materials by name lets a skin change be a set of `color.setHex` calls — no model rebuild, no disposal churn, no per-frame cost. New tests: `createPlayerModel(zombiePalette)` → `paletteMaterials.skin.color.getHex() === 0x6a9a4e`; `applyPalette` swaps colors on the *same* material instances (capture refs before/after) and allocates nothing (`materials.length` unchanged); `paletteMaterials` values are all contained in `materials`. playerVisuals: `visuals.setPalette(robot)` then assert a mesh material color through the scene. Existing 4 model tests pass untouched (default param). **Slice 3 — `Generate 16x16 bust portraits for skin presets`** Files: `lib/ui/skinPortrait.ts`, `lib/ui/skinPortrait.test.ts`, `lib/ui/sprites.ts`. Why-body: the picker needs a face for each preset; deriving a pixel bust from the same palette that colors the 3D body keeps the zero-asset guarantee and makes the swatch automatically truthful for any future preset. Tests (mirror `spritePixels.test.ts` integrity style): every preset yields a 16×16×4 buffer with >40 opaque pixels; deterministic; all six pairwise distinct; hair rows (y=1..3) use the hair color and shoulder rows (y=13..14) the shirt color for a known preset. **Slice 4 — `Add an Appearance picker to the pause menu`** Files: `PauseMenu.tsx`, `PauseMenu.test.tsx`, `MinecraftGame.tsx`, `useMinecraftGame.ts`, `app/hud.css`, `e2e/smoke.e2e.ts` (or a new `e2e` spec), `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/adding-content.md`. Why-body: surfaces the presets where players already manage preferences; selection applies live through the renderer (same path audio settings take to the director) and persists outside the world save so it survives resets. # Player Skin Presets (Appearance Picker)

## Context

The third-person player body (shipped in PR #9) has its palette burned in as seven module constants in `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`. This feature lets players pick their character's look from six classic preset palettes — **Default** (current colors), **Alex** (pale skin, orange hair, green shirt), **Zombie**, **Skeleton**, **Knight** (steel tones, dark visor eye band), **Robot** (gunmetal, glowing cyan eyes) — from a new "Appearance" section in the pause menu, with a generated 16×16 pixel-art bust portrait per preset.

Key decisions (made with the user): all six presets ship; portraits are pixel busts via the existing zero-asset sprite system. Design constraints: skin choice is a **player preference, not world state** — own localStorage key (`minecraft_skin_v1`) mirroring the audio settings pattern, never engine state or save data; selection applies **live** via `material.color.setHex()` (no model rebuild); colors only in v1 (same geometry for all presets).

Branch: `feature/player-skins` off `main`.

## Design

### New: `lib/game/playerSkins.ts` — presets (pure)

```ts
export type PlayerPalette = { skin; hair; shirt; pants; shoes; eyeWhite; eyePupil: number };
export type SkinId = "default" | "alex" | "zombie" | "skeleton" | "knight" | "robot";
export type SkinPreset = { id: SkinId; label: string; palette: PlayerPalette };
export const DEFAULT_SKIN_ID: SkinId = "default";
export const DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE: PlayerPalette;  // alias of the default preset's palette
export const SKIN_PRESETS: readonly SkinPreset[];
export function isSkinId(value: unknown): value is SkinId;
export function getSkinPreset(id: string): SkinPreset;  // unknown id → default preset
```

# Camera View Toggle: First-Person / Third-Person (Rear & Front)

## Context

Add a Minecraft-F5-style camera cycle: **V** key switches first-person → third-person rear (camera behind the player) → third-person front (camera facing the player) → back to first. Today the game is first-person only — the camera is rebuilt each frame from `player.yaw/pitch` + `EYE_HEIGHT`, and there is no player body mesh (only a held-item overlay parented to the camera).

The architecture makes this a presentation-layer feature: mining, placing, combat, movement, and audio panning all read player yaw/pitch/eye position from engine state, never the Three.js camera, so gameplay stays eye-relative and untouched in every mode. The two real work items are a humanoid player body (visible only in third person) and camera wall-clamping so the third-person camera never sees through blocks.

Decisions already made with the user: **V** key (not F5 — browser refresh conflict), **proper humanoid model** (head, torso, 2 arms, 2 legs, walk-swing animation, held item shown in hand). View mode is session-only (not saved), like the debug overlay.

Branch: `feature/camera-view-toggle` off `main`.

## Design

### View mode in engine state (mirrors `toggleDebug`)

- `lib/game/engine/state.ts`: `export type CameraMode = "first" | "third-rear" | "third-front"`, a `nextCameraMode()` cycle helper, `GameState.cameraMode` + `GameSnapshot.cameraMode` (init `"first"`).
- `lib/game/engine/commands.ts`: `{ type: "toggleCameraView" }`; unconditional dispatch case in `GameEngine.ts` (works while dead/paused — render-only, like Minecraft).
- `lib/game/useMinecraftGame.ts`: add `cameraMode: "first"` to `PRE_MOUNT_SNAPSHOT`.
- `lib/game/input/inputController.ts`: `KeyV` → dispatch, placed next to the F3 handler.
- `serialize()` is untouched → session-only persistence for free. No save-format impact.

### Camera math (`lib/game/render/cameraView.ts`, new, pure — testable like `heldItemPose.ts`)

Conventions (verified): forward at yaw=0 is **−Z** (`lookDirection` in playerMotion.ts), camera rotation order YXZ, positive pitch = up.

- **Rear**: camera = eye − look·d; rotation `(yaw, pitch)` unchanged.
- **Front**: camera = eye + look·d; rotation `(yaw + π, −pitch)` — the camera faces back at the player; mouse input is untouched (`applyLook` unchanged), so horizontal motion appears mirrored on screen, which is authentic Minecraft F5 behavior.
- Exports: `cameraOffsetDirection(mode, yaw, pitch, out)` and `computeCameraPose(mode, eyeX, eyeY, eyeZ, yaw, pitch, distance)`.

**Wall clamp** in `GameRenderer.syncCamera` for third-person modes: raycast eye → offset direction with the existing `voxelRaycast` (`lib/world/queries.ts:11`), clamp `distance = hit ? max(0, hit.distance − THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN) : THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`. Requires extending `RaycastResult` with `distance: number` — the DDA loop variable `t` at `queries.ts:38` is exactly the hit-cell entry parameter; return it. Renderer already reads world data, so importing `voxelRaycast` there is architecturally fine. Use module-scope scratch `Vector3`s (existing pattern).

Constants in `lib/game/config.ts`: `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE = 4`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN = 0.2` (> near plane 0.1).

Fog, chunk culling (player-position-keyed), crack overlay (world-space), and audio (player-yaw-based) all verified unaffected.

### Player body (new files under `lib/game/render/`, mirroring the mob-visuals split)

- **`playerModel.ts`** — box-geometry humanoid factory, vertex-color materials, zero binary assets (Steve-ish palette: skin/shirt/pants constants in-file). **Face built on the −Z side** so `group.rotation.y = player.yaw` matches the camera convention (the mob model faces +Z — don't copy blindly). Limbs are pivot `Group`s at shoulder/hip with the mesh offset −length/2, so `rotation.x` swings naturally. Returns `{ group, head, leftArm, rightArm, leftLeg, rightLeg, itemHolder, materials, geometries }`. Suggested dims (PLAYER_HEIGHT 1.8, eye ≈ 1.62): legs 0.2×0.72×0.2, torso 0.46×0.6×0.24 (y 0.72–1.32), arms 0.16×0.66×0.16 at shoulders y 1.26, head 0.4 cube on neck pivot y 1.32; tune in the manual pass.
- **`playerPose.ts`** — pure, no Three.js: `computePlayerPose({ timeMs, moveFactor, miningActive, swingStartMs })` → limb `rotation.x` values. Walk gait `sin(timeMs·0.012)·0.8·moveFactor`, legs counter-phased, arms counter-phased to same-side legs; right-arm chop overlay reusing the `heldItemPose.ts` swing-timing idiom (one-shot ~260 ms, looping while mining).
- **`playerVisuals.ts`** — renderer view `{ sync(state, timeMs), triggerSwing(), dispose() }`. `sync`: `group.visible = state.cameraMode !== "first" && !state.isDead`; position at feet, `rotation.y = yaw`, pitch on the **head only**; `moveFactor` computed exactly as `GameRenderer.sync` does for the held item (GameRenderer.ts:97); held item rebuilt into `itemHolder` on `slot.id` change (track-and-dispose like `heldItem.ts:72-86`).
- **`itemModel.ts`** (new) — extract `heldItem.ts`'s `buildModel`/`blockColor` (lines ~50-68: block → cube, else extruded sprite) into a shared `buildItemModel(slot)`; consumed by both `heldItem.ts` and `playerVisuals.ts`, each disposing what it built.

### First-person overlay hiding

Add `visible: boolean` to `HeldItemFrame`; `heldItem.update` sets `root.visible` and skips pose work when hidden. `GameRenderer.sync` passes `visible: state.cameraMode === "first"`. `GameRenderer.triggerSwing()` fans out to both heldItem and playerVisuals.

## Commit slices (each keeps lint + tests green)

1. **Add distance to voxelRaycast results** — `lib/world/queries.ts` + test (ray toward a block N cells away → expected distance). Why-body: third-person camera needs the ray parameter to clamp against walls; existing callers ignore the field.
2. **Add camera view mode state with a V-key cycle command** — state.ts, commands.ts, GameEngine.ts, useMinecraftGame.ts, inputController.ts + GameEngine tests (cycle order, default `"first"`, `serialize()` output has no camera field, snapshot notifies).
3. **Extract shared held-item model building** — `itemModel.ts`, refactor `heldItem.ts` onto it; existing heldItem tests stay green + small itemModel test. Pure extraction, no behavior change.
4. **Add humanoid player body model with walk and swing animation** — `playerModel.ts`, `playerPose.ts`, `playerVisuals.ts` + tests (parts/disposal à la mobVisuals tests; gait scales with moveFactor; hidden in `"first"`; item swaps on slot change).
5. **Render third-person camera views with wall clamping** — `cameraView.ts` + test (rear passthrough yaw/pitch; front yaw+π / −pitch), config constants, `GameRenderer.ts` wiring (syncCamera branch, clamp, playerVisuals, heldItem visible flag, swing fan-out), e2e smoke addition.
6. **Document the V camera view toggle** — README controls, `components/game/PauseMenu.tsx` CONTROLS array (~line 14-24, check PauseMenu tests), CHANGELOG entry ("no save-format or worldgen impact"), docs/testing.md coverage row, docs/architecture.md if it lists GameState fields/render modules.

## Verification

- **Unit**: per-slice tests above; engine test is the spec for cycling/session-only; cameraView test is the spec for front-view inversion.
- **E2E** (`e2e/smoke.e2e.ts`): press `v` → `engine.state.cameraMode === "third-rear"` and `renderedTriangles() > 0`; two more presses → `"third-front"` then `"first"`. Document-level keydown — no pointer lock needed.
- **Manual gameplay pass** (required — visual + pointer-lock-adjacent, per docs/testing.md): body faces look direction; limbs swing while walking, idle when still; right arm chops on mining/attack; held item in hand matches hotbar; overlay hidden in third person and restored cleanly; rear camera clamps against a wall behind (front view: wall ahead); front view tilt feels like Minecraft F5; dying in third person doesn't leave a floating body; pause/inventory/F3 work in all modes; crosshair stays centered (intentional, matches Minecraft — note in PR).
- **Baseline before PR**: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, `bun test`, `bun run build`, `bun run test:e2e`.

## Branch & PR (user-authorized)

All work on `feature/camera-view-toggle` off `main`, committed in the six slices above. Once the full verification baseline is green, push the branch and open a PR against this fork's `main` (`gh pr create --repo hutusi/monecraft --base main`), no AI-attribution lines in the description. The PR description will note: gameplay raycasts/audio intentionally unchanged (eye-relative in all modes), crosshair stays centered in third person (matches Minecraft), no save-format or worldgen impact, and that the manual gameplay pass items above should be checked in-browser before merge.

# Player Skin Presets (Appearance Picker)

## Context

The third-person player body (shipped in PR #9) has its palette burned in as seven module constants in `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`. This feature lets players pick their character's look from six classic preset palettes — **Default** (current colors), **Alex** (pale skin, orange hair, green shirt), **Zombie**, **Skeleton**, **Knight** (steel tones, dark visor eye band), **Robot** (gunmetal, glowing cyan eyes) — from a new "Appearance" section in the pause menu, with a generated 16×16 pixel-art bust portrait per preset.

Key decisions (made with the user): all six presets ship; portraits are pixel busts via the existing zero-asset sprite system. Design constraints: skin choice is a **player preference, not world state** — own localStorage key (`minecraft_skin_v1`) mirroring the audio settings pattern, never engine state or save data; selection applies **live** via `material.color.setHex()` (no model rebuild); colors only in v1 (same geometry for all presets).

Branch: `feature/player-skins` off `main`.

## Design

export type SkinId = "default" | "alex" | "zombie" | "skeleton" | "knight" | "robot";
export type SkinPreset = { id: SkinId; label: string; palette: PlayerPalette };
export const DEFAULT_SKIN_ID: SkinId = "default";
export const DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE: PlayerPalette;  // alias of the default preset's palette
export const SKIN_PRESETS: readonly SkinPreset[];
export function isSkinId(value: unknown): value is SkinId;
export function getSkinPreset(id: string): SkinPreset;  // unknown id → default preset
```

Palettes (hex):

| preset | skin | hair | shirt | pants | shoes | eyeWhite | eyePupil |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | c68e63 | 4a3220 | 2e8b83 | 3b3f8f | 4a3527 | ffffff | 2b2b45 |
| Alex | e6b18a | b5602e | 5f8a3a | 6e5036 | 57422c | ffffff | 3f6b3a |
| Zombie | 6a9a4e | 4e7a3a | 2f6e62 | 4f4377 | 3d3326 | 1d2b1d | 0a120a |
| Skeleton | dcdcd2 | c4c4ba | b1b1a7 | 9a9a90 | 83837a | 2e2e2e | 121212 |
| Knight | aab2bd | 7c8591 | 8d96a3 | 646d79 | 4a525c | 161a20 | 161a20 |
| Robot | 767f8a | 4d545e | 5b636d | 444b54 | 32373e | 35e9ff | 0b6f80 |

Knight's eyeWhite == eyePupil intentionally reads as a continuous dark visor slit. Robot's bright cyan eyeWhite reads as a glow (true emissive is a deliberate v2 omission — keeps `setPalette` color-only).

### New: `lib/game/skinSettings.ts` — persistence (mirror `lib/game/audio/settings.ts`)

`SKIN_SETTINGS_KEY = "minecraft_skin_v1"`, `SkinSettings = { skinId: SkinId }` (object for forward-compat), `readSkinSettings(storage = localStorage)` with try/catch + `isSkinId` validation → default fallback, `writeSkinSettings` with silent quota-failure catch.

- Drop the 7 color constants; `createPlayerModel(palette: PlayerPalette = DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE)` — default param keeps all existing call sites/tests untouched.
- Extend `PlayerModel` with `paletteMaterials: Record<keyof PlayerPalette, THREE.MeshStandardMaterial>` (same instances also stay in `materials`, which remains the sole disposal authority).
- New `export function applyPalette(model, palette)` — `color.setHex()` per key; allocates nothing.

- `PlayerVisuals.setPalette(palette)` → `applyPalette(model, palette)`.
- `GameRenderer.setPlayerSkin(palette)` next to `triggerSwing()` — renderer stays id-agnostic; the hook resolves id → palette.
- No constructor param for the initial palette: the renderer effect calls `setPlayerSkin` synchronously after `GameRenderer.create`, before the first rAF, and the body boots invisible (first-person), so no default-palette flash is possible.

- `updateSkin(id)` callback: set ref + state, `writeSkinSettings({ skinId: id })`, `rendererRef.current?.setPlayerSkin(...)`. Return `skinId, updateSkin`.

`renderSkinPortraitPixels(palette): Uint8ClampedArray` — 16×16 pixel bust (hair rows, skin face with eyeWhite/pupil pixels, neck with shadow shades via a `shade(rgb, 0.75)` helper, shirt shoulders) using `paintGrid` from `lib/ui/spritePixels.ts`. Add to `lib/ui/sprites.ts`:

Existing model tests pass via the default param.

5. **Document the skin presets** — README features/controls note, CHANGELOG entry ("session preference under `minecraft_skin_v1`; no save-format or worldgen impact"), `docs/adding-content.md` "Adding a skin preset" note, docs/testing.md + docs/architecture.md rows.

# Player Skin Presets (Appearance Picker)

## Context

The third-person player body (shipped in PR #9) has its palette burned in as seven module constants in `lib/game/render/playerModel.ts`. This feature lets players pick their character's look from six classic preset palettes — **Default** (current colors), **Alex** (pale skin, orange hair, green shirt), **Zombie**, **Skeleton**, **Knight** (steel tones, dark visor eye band), **Robot** (gunmetal, glowing cyan eyes) — from a new "Appearance" section in the pause menu, with a generated 16×16 pixel-art bust portrait per preset.

Key decisions (made with the user): all six presets ship; portraits are pixel busts via the existing zero-asset sprite system. Design constraints: skin choice is a **player preference, not world state** — own localStorage key (`minecraft_skin_v1`) mirroring the audio settings pattern, never engine state or save data; selection applies **live** via `material.color.setHex()` (no model rebuild); colors only in v1 (same geometry for all presets).

Branch: `feature/player-skins` off `main`.

export type SkinId = "default" | "alex" | "zombie" | "skeleton" | "knight" | "robot";
export type SkinPreset = { id: SkinId; label: string; palette: PlayerPalette };
export const DEFAULT_SKIN_ID: SkinId = "default";
export const DEFAULT_PLAYER_PALETTE: PlayerPalette;  // alias of the default preset's palette
export const SKIN_PRESETS: readonly SkinPreset[];
export function isSkinId(value: unknown): value is SkinId;
export function getSkinPreset(id: string): SkinPreset;  // unknown id → default preset
```

| preset | skin | hair | shirt | pants | shoes | eyeWhite | eyePupil |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | c68e63 | 4a3220 | 2e8b83 | 3b3f8f | 4a3527 | ffffff | 2b2b45 |
| Alex | e6b18a | b5602e | 5f8a3a | 6e5036 | 57422c | ffffff | 3f6b3a |
| Zombie | 6a9a4e | 4e7a3a | 2f6e62 | 4f4377 | 3d3326 | 1d2b1d | 0a120a |
